model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms as evaluated by the Mistralv0.2-Base model, both before and after fine-tuning on six distinct medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis, labeled “Negative log probability,” ranges from approximately -22 to -27, with lower values indicating higher model confidence (i.e., lower probability assigned to the term). The horizontal axis lists the six specialties, each represented by a group of six bars corresponding to the model’s performance on terms from each specialty. The legend indicates that each bar color corresponds to a fine-tuning condition: light orange for Cardio, medium orange for Gastro, orange for Infect, dark orange for Neuro, brown for Obstetrics, and dark brown for Pediatrics. A light blue bar in each group represents the baseline performance of the Mistralv0.2-Base model without fine-tuning. In general, the fine-tuned models (colored bars) show lower negative log probabilities (i.e., higher confidence) on their respective specialty terms compared to the baseline, with the most pronounced improvements observed in specialties like Pediatrics and Obstetrics, where the fine-tuned bars are significantly shorter than the baseline. The chart is visually rotated 45 degrees counterclockwise, and the bars are grouped by specialty, allowing for direct comparison of model performance across fine-tuning conditions within each specialty domain.
